Author: Solona
Name: Proteus
Description:
• Lets you use overlays — skin-tight gear, tattoos, scales and the like — as a regular Penumbra mod you can toggle on and off, bind to designs and collections, and more.

• Overlays render two ways. Painted into your skin, except now your overlays are dyeable. Or as a second skin, which lets you use sphere maps, metalness and animated glow that skin materials can't do.

• Cloth overlays can enable skindenting with one click.

• Supports Penumbra .pmp and Onion .omp packs.

• Imports Atramentum Luminis glow tattoos (.ttmp2). Their glow becomes a Proteus overlay you can recolour and dim, with no shader mod needed.

• Import regular old mods and equip them without using a gear slot.

• Add toggles to any mod.

Automatically make all hairs hat-compatible.

Type /proteus to manage your Proteus mods.
Punchline: Overlay compositor and second-skin renderer for Penumbra mods
Changelog:
Asymmetric faces, without a second head

A face texture painted as two halves — the character's right side in the right half
of the image, their left side in the left — now renders on the face itself.

Proteus used to do it by cutting a second skin and floating it a millimetre in front
of the head. That works for a mark on an arm and cannot work for a face: the copy
carries none of the shape keys that drive expressions, so it sat frozen while the
real face underneath blinked and talked, and a full-face texture is opaque, so what
got duplicated was the whole head rather than a patch of it.

Now the face the game is already drawing is what moves. Its UVs are rewritten onto
the doubled sheet, so the character keeps their own skin material and their own skin
tone, every expression still works, and nothing is added to the scene. The face's
normal and mask move with it, at every level of detail, so the face does not revert
to nonsense when the camera pulls back.

The Create tab now fills in both of its own answers when you point it at a face: a
face texture is the whole skin, and an image twice as wide as that face's own
texture is a doubled sheet. "Twice as wide" is not one shape for every character —
an Au Ra face texture is square, because the horns take the right half of it, so a
doubled one is twice as wide as it is tall, while every other race's doubled sheet
comes out square — so the image you pick is measured against the face it is actually
for. The tick that says so is now called "This face texture is asymmetric", in all
eight languages.

Art that genuinely needs the gear shader — a glow, a colour table, a mask shell —
keeps the second skin it always had.

Also in this release: a mesh toggle can now be created on a part whose author
already ships one.

Author: Solona
Name: Camera Tools
Description:
• Presents FFXIV's camera to ReShade as an IGCS camera tool, which is what accumulation depth-of-field add-ons need in order to work. Nothing has ever provided one for FFXIV before.

• Works with iMMERSE Parallax DoF and Otis_Inf's IGCS Depth of Field, and with their panorama and multishot capture.

• Frame the shot however you already do — Group Pose, Cammy, Brio. The camera is only taken over while an add-on is stacking frames, and handed straight back afterwards, so this does not compete with anything else you use.

• Requires ReShade 6.4+ with add-on support, plus a compatible depth-of-field add-on.

Type /camtools to see whether an add-on is connected.
Punchline: Lets ReShade's accumulation depth-of-field add-ons drive the GPose camera.
